title: REIS: A High-Performance and Energy-Efficient Retrieval System with In-Storage Processing
problem: The retrieval stage of RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a throughput bottleneck because Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) on large embedding databases incurs massive data movement between host and storage; existing In-Storage Processing (ISP) approaches use storage-agnostic ANNS algorithms, do not accelerate the subsequent data-fetch step, and require heavy SSD hardware modifications.
motivation: LLMs have static knowledge cutoffs and retraining is prohibitively expensive; RAG is the practical solution, but its retrieval stage can dominate end-to-end inference latency at scale, making storage-side acceleration critical for production deployments.
method: REIS co-designs the ANNS algorithm with ISP hardware inside the storage system to avoid host-storage data movement. It adopts an ISP-tailored ANNS algorithm that exploits the internal bandwidth and parallelism of NAND flash controllers without large hardware modifications. REIS additionally accelerates the data-retrieval step for items selected by ANNS, overlapping fetch and search computations. The system is designed to minimize changes to storage hardware while maximizing throughput.
key_novelty: ISP-tailored ANNS algorithm that co-designs the search procedure with the flash storage controller's internal architecture, simultaneously accelerating both vector search and subsequent data retrieval without significant hardware modification.
contributions: ISP-optimized ANNS algorithm tailored to the internal bandwidth and parallelism of flash storage controllers
Acceleration of the post-ANNS data retrieval step, which prior ISP works leave on the critical path
Near-storage system design that requires minimal hardware modifications to existing SSD architectures
High-performance, energy-efficient retrieval system enabling faster RAG pipelines for LLMs

metrics.other: High performance and energy efficiency claimed; specific numbers not reported in abstract

limitations: Not discussed in abstract; hardware modification scope and ANNS accuracy-recall tradeoffs under ISP constraints are not quantified.
primary_theme: in-storage processing for RAG retrieval acceleration
